chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hammad al-Nab, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who married a woman upon a known orchard belonging to him, and it had abundant produce; then he remained for years without consummating the marriage, then he divorced her.

He عليه السلام said: He must consider what produce the orchard has come to yield from the day he married her, then give her half of it, and give her half of the orchard, unless she waives it, accepts something from him, and the two come to an agreement upon something with which she is pleased from him.
For that is nearer to taqwa.

key_terms.بُسْتَانٍ: an orchard given as the specified mahr in the marriage contract
key_terms.غَلَّةٌ: the produce or yield generated by the orchard
key_terms.لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: he did not consummate the marriage with her
key_terms.لِلتَّقْوَىٰ: to piety or God-conscious restraint in settling rights
key_terms.نِصْفَ الْبُسْتَانِ: half ownership of the orchard owed to her
key_terms.نِصْفَهُ: half of the orchard's produce owed to her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman is divorced before consummation when her mahr was an orchard with produce?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a marriage in which the mahr was a specified orchard and the husband later divorced the wife before consummation. It states that she is entitled to half of the orchard and half of its produce accrued from the time of marriage, unless she willingly remits part of it and they mutually settle on an acceptable agreement, which is described as closer to taqwa.
